11:15.topic: What college coaches evaluate in a catcher
11:15.alt_text: A young baseball catcher in full gear crouches behind the plate on a sunny field, ready for the pitch.
11:15.headline: Catchers: more than a pop time
11:15.caption:
Pop time gets the headlines. Coaches watch everything that happens before and after the throw.

If your son catches, here's what college staffs tend to evaluate:

⚾ Receiving. Does he catch the low strike quietly and give the umpire a clean look?
⚾ Blocking. Can he keep balls in the dirt in front of him with runners on?
⚾ Throwing. Pop time is the glove-to-glove time on a throw to second. Accuracy counts as much as speed.
⚾ Running the game. How he works with pitchers, sets up hitters and talks to the infield.
⚾ The bat. A catcher who can hit adds a lot of value to a lineup.

Coaches often trust a catcher who receives and blocks well over one with a big arm and stiff hands.

Catcher parents: which of these is your son working on this winter? 👇 Save this for his next skills video.
